summary: T18 pins the T11 deployment defect - `docker stop` on the running relay reports `Exited (2)`, so an ordinary operator stop is indistinguishable from a crash - with FOUR new Go tests in ONE new file, apps/relay/internal/server/process_shutdown_test.go (sha256 c38372f5ff4a983d6ad39799dfda28e36e5d9e8625131094222bc5eb08329155). Nothing else in the tree was created, edited, weakened, narrowed, skipped or deleted; `git status --porcelain -- apps packages docs` shows exactly one new file under apps/ (the four modified docs/ files are pre-existing, listed in the T11 report's own dirty list, and were not touched). All four tests drive the REAL cmd/relay binary as a REAL child process, because signal disposition is a property of the process: main.go installs no signal handler at all, so an in-process test of a handler or of *server.Server would pass while the shipped binary is still torn down by the kernel. The binary is built with `go build -o <t.TempDir()>/relay-under-test ./cmd/relay` and never written into the repository tree. (1) TestRelayExitsZeroOnSIGTERM - a SIGTERMed relay must exit 0 within 10 s. RED: 'relay exited signal: terminated after SIGTERM, want exit status 0 (ExitCode()==-1)'. (2) TestRelayExitsZeroOnSIGINT - same for Ctrl-C on a foreground relay. RED: 'relay exited signal: interrupt after SIGINT, want exit status 0 (ExitCode()==-1)'. (3) TestRelayDrainsInFlightRequestOnSIGTERM - a request the server has already begun serving must complete, and no new connection may be accepted after the signal. RED: 'the in-flight request was cut by SIGTERM: no response was read back: unexpected EOF'. (4) TestRelayClosesStorageCleanlyOnSIGTERM - Badger must be closed, not abandoned, so the next start is an ordinary open and not a value-log replay. RED: 'storage was not closed cleanly on SIGTERM: memtable write-ahead log(s) [00001.mem] remain in <dir>'. SYNCHRONISATION, which is the substance of the task: there is no sleep-until-probably-ready anywhere. Readiness is /health answering 200 on a reserved loopback port (the binary logs "Starting relay server" BEFORE it binds, so the log line alone would not prove the port is open). 'A request is in flight' is proved by `Expect: 100-continue`: net/http emits the interim `100 Continue` only once the handler first reads r.Body - for POST /v1/mailbox/challenge that is decodeJSONRequest - so reading that line is positive proof the handler is running and blocked on a body the test has deliberately not sent yet; SIGTERM is sent only after that line is read, and the body is sent only after the signal. 'The listener is gone' is a real dial being refused, polled to a bound, and it is checked WHILE the in-flight request is still held open, so it is a statement about the shutdown sequence rather than about a dead process. 'The process is finished' is cmd.Wait returning. The 10 s bound is justified in a comment from the deployment and not from taste: `docker stop` SIGKILLs after a 10 s grace period by default, so a relay needing longer is killed by Docker and reports non-zero for that reason alone; a correct idle shutdown needs milliseconds, so a failure at that bound is a real hang. The storage observable was established empirically with a throwaway probe test that was deleted afterwards (tree verified clean): while Badger is open the directory holds `00001.mem` and `LOCK`; a clean Close flushes the memtable into an SST, deletes the .mem file and releases the lock. The test asserts BOTH files are present while the relay runs (a precondition, so the post-condition cannot pass vacuously) and both are gone after exit. Test (4) deliberately does NOT assert the exit status and test (3) deliberately does not either, so each failure can only mean its own property. SUITE COUNTS after these tests. Go, `go -C apps/relay test ./...`: 87 top-level PASS, 4 FAIL, 0 SKIP - the 4 failures are exactly the 4 new tests and no other package changed colour (api/handler, api/router, config, middleware, storage/repository, tlsx, validation all ok). `-race` and `-race -tags relayv2` each show the SAME 4 failures, every other package ok, and 0 DATA RACE in both. `go vet ./internal/server/` exit 0, so nothing fails on a compile error. `pnpm test` 293/293 passed across 7 projects (protocol 12, client-db 1, crypto-core 20, client-core 2, session-node 24, mobile 6, cli 228) - unchanged from the baseline. `pnpm --filter @echolet/cli test:e2e` 3/3 passed (the root has no test:e2e script; it lives in apps/cli/package.json). `pnpm typecheck` exit 0. Run on Node v26.5.0, the default non-login interpreter. NO production change was needed or made: everything these tests assert is observable from outside the process.

acceptance.criterion: The relay process, sent SIGTERM, exits with status 0 within a bounded time, and the bound is justified in a comment.
acceptance.evidence: TestRelayExitsZeroOnSIGTERM (process_shutdown_test.go:66). RED today: 'relay exited signal: terminated after SIGTERM, want exit status 0 (ExitCode()==-1); a normal operator stop must not look like a crash.' The bound is the package constant shutdownBudget = 10s, justified in its comment from `docker stop`'s default 10 s SIGTERM grace before SIGKILL (a relay slower than that is killed by Docker and reports non-zero for that reason alone) and from the fact that a correct idle shutdown - closing a listener with no active connections and closing Badger - takes milliseconds, so a failure at the bound is a real hang and not a slow machine. The failure is on the assertion, not on the bound: the process is gone in under 2 s in every run.

acceptance.criterion: It shuts down gracefully: an HTTP request already in flight when SIGTERM arrives is allowed to complete rather than being cut, and no new connection is accepted after the signal.
acceptance.evidence: TestRelayDrainsInFlightRequestOnSIGTERM (process_shutdown_test.go:112). RED today at line 167: 'the in-flight request was cut by SIGTERM: no response was read back: unexpected EOF; an already-accepted request must be allowed to complete.' The in-flight half is genuine, not assumed: the client writes only the request head of POST /v1/mailbox/challenge with `Expect: 100-continue` and `Content-Length`, then BLOCKS until the server writes `HTTP/1.1 100 Continue` - which net/http emits only when the handler first reads r.Body - and only then sends SIGTERM, and only after that sends the body. The failure output proves the sequence worked: the interim line was read (so the handler was provably running), the body write succeeded, and the response was the thing that never arrived. The 'no new connection' half is asserted in the same test, while the in-flight request is still held, via dialRefusedWithin polling a real dial. That half PASSES on the current tree - a dead process refuses connections too - so it is correctly an in-test guard on the fix rather than a standalone RED; a fix that closes storage and exits 0 but keeps accepting during the drain turns it red.

acceptance.criterion: The storage layer is closed cleanly before exit, asserted on something observable rather than on a sleep.
acceptance.evidence: TestRelayClosesStorageCleanlyOnSIGTERM (process_shutdown_test.go:191). RED today at line 213: 'storage was not closed cleanly on SIGTERM: memtable write-ahead log(s) [00001.mem] remain in <tmp>/relay-data. A clean badger.Close flushes and deletes them; leaving them turns every ordinary stop into a value-log replay on the next start.' The observable is Badger's own on-disk footprint, established empirically rather than assumed: a throwaway probe test (since deleted) showed the directory holds 000001.vlog, 00001.mem, DISCARD, KEYREGISTRY, LOCK, MANIFEST while open, and 000001.vlog, DISCARD, KEYREGISTRY, MANIFEST after a clean Close - the .mem memtable WAL and the LOCK file are both removed. The test asserts both are PRESENT while the relay runs (an explicit precondition with its own failure message, so the post-condition cannot pass vacuously) and both are ABSENT after the process has exited, waiting on cmd.Wait rather than on a delay. It deliberately does not assert the exit status, so a failure here can only mean the store was not closed.

acceptance.criterion: SIGINT behaves the same as SIGTERM, because Ctrl-C is how an operator stops a foreground relay.
acceptance.evidence: TestRelayExitsZeroOnSIGINT (process_shutdown_test.go:84), the same assertion and the same bound as the SIGTERM case. RED today: 'relay exited signal: interrupt after SIGINT, want exit status 0 (ExitCode()==-1); Ctrl-C on a foreground relay must be a clean stop.'

acceptance.criterion: Every new test is RED for the right reason - failing on its assertion, not on a compile error, a missing fixture or a timeout that would fire regardless.
acceptance.evidence: `go -C apps/relay vet ./internal/server/` exits 0, so nothing fails to compile. Each of the four failures is a t.Fatalf on the property's own assertion, quoted above, and each names what it saw. None is a budget expiry: every run finished in 1.2-2.5 s against a 10 s budget, and the two budgets that are not assertions (startupBudget 30 s, ioBudget 15 s) were never reached - startup completed and the interim 100-Continue line arrived in every run. The four are also mutually non-overlapping: the drain test and the storage test deliberately do not assert the exit status, so no failure is a duplicate of another test's reason.

acceptance.criterion: Tests must be deterministic: synchronise on an observable event, never on a sleep long enough to probably work.
acceptance.evidence: Four observable events, no probabilistic waits. Readiness = /health returning 200 on a reserved loopback port, retried on a 10 ms poll (the binary logs 'Starting relay server' BEFORE net.Listen, so the log line would have been the wrong signal - noted in the code). In-flight = the server's `100 Continue` interim response, which net/http emits only when the handler begins reading the body. Listener closed = a real dial being refused, retried on a 10 ms poll to a bound. Exit = cmd.Wait returning, delivered over a channel and selected against a timer. The only time.Sleep calls in the file are the 10 ms retry intervals inside those two poll loops; no sleep stands in for an event. The relay is given an explicit, minimal environment rather than the developer's, so a stray ECHOLET_* variable in the shell cannot change what is under test, and the port is reserved by binding and releasing 127.0.0.1:0 so two concurrent runs cannot collide.

acceptance.criterion: TESTS ONLY. No change under apps/relay/internal except *_test.go, nothing under apps/relay/cmd, apps/cli, packages/ or docs/. Nothing existing weakened, skipped, narrowed or deleted.
acceptance.evidence: Exactly one file was created: apps/relay/internal/server/process_shutdown_test.go, a *_test.go in an existing package. `git status --porcelain -- apps packages docs` reports it as the only untracked entry under apps/ and no modification anywhere under apps/ or packages/; the four modified files under docs/ are pre-existing and are the same four the T11 deployment report lists in its own dirty set. No production change was needed - every property here is observable from outside the process - so the 'stop rather than change production code' escape hatch was not used. A throwaway probe test in internal/storage was created to measure Badger's clean-close footprint and deleted immediately; it appears in no diff.

acceptance.criterion: Baseline preserved and reported; state exactly which failures are ours.
acceptance.evidence: Go `go -C apps/relay test ./...`: 87 top-level PASS / 4 FAIL / 0 SKIP; `-race`: same 4 failures, 0 DATA RACE; `-race -tags relayv2`: same 4 failures, 0 DATA RACE. In all three configurations api/handler, api/router, config, middleware, storage/repository, tlsx and validation are ok. The four failures are TestRelayExitsZeroOnSIGTERM, TestRelayExitsZeroOnSIGINT, TestRelayDrainsInFlightRequestOnSIGTERM and TestRelayClosesStorageCleanlyOnSIGTERM - all four are mine, and they are the only failures in the module. JS is untouched and unchanged from the baseline: `pnpm test` 293/293 (protocol 12, client-db 1, crypto-core 20, client-core 2, session-node 24, mobile 6, cli 228), `pnpm --filter @echolet/cli test:e2e` 3/3, `pnpm typecheck` exit 0. Node v26.5.0.

acceptance.criterion: Do not print or record any store key, private key, plaintext or HTTP request body; do not touch or connect to geekom or depr.
acceptance.evidence: The only request body in the tests is a fixed literal placeholder ({"recipient_mailbox_id":"drain-probe","device_id":"drain-probe","signature":"drain-probe"}); it carries no key, no identity and no plaintext, and the test asserts only that a complete HTTP response arrives, never on its contents - the response body is read into io.Discard-equivalent and discarded. No key material of any kind is generated, read or logged. Everything runs on 127.0.0.1 against a freshly built binary and an empty t.TempDir() data directory; no host other than loopback is contacted, and neither geekom nor depr was connected to at any point.

artifacts.summary: Four process-level shutdown tests driving the real cmd/relay binary: exit 0 on SIGTERM, exit 0 on SIGINT, in-flight request drained and listener closed after SIGTERM, Badger closed cleanly before exit. Plus the harness: build into a temp dir, reserve a loopback port, wait on /health, signal, wait on cmd.Wait.
